simple.meaning: זָרַר (zârar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “perhaps to diffuse , i.e. (specifically) to sneeze.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 2 Kings, beginning at 2 Kings 4:35. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָרַר (H2237) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זָרַר (zârar) / H2237 is traced through 2 Kings 4:35 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: perhaps to diffuse , i.e. (specifically) to sneeze
definitions.full: H2237. zarar [ זָרַר ] verb only Po`el sneeze (compare ᵑ7 זְרִירוֺ(ה)י Job 41:10 for Hebrew עֲטִישֹׁתָיו ; verb probably onomatopoetic); — פעמים֯ שׁבע עד הַנַּעַר וַיְזוֺרֵר 2Kin 4:35 **omitted ᵐ5 ; Gr Bur think MT arose (by dittograph) from עַלהַֿנַּעַר וַיִּגְהַר .

occurrences.englishText: Then he returned, and walked in the house once back and forth; and went up, and stretched himself out on him. Then the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
